claims.text: Parent and adolescent reports of adolescent social media account counts are moderately correlated with parent-reported DSM-5 symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity, ODD, anxiety, and depression.
Parent and adolescent reports of adolescent social media account counts are moderately correlated with adolescent-reported fear of missing out (FoMO) and loneliness.
Adolescent anxiety and depressive symptoms are highest among adolescents with both a relatively high number of parent-reported social media accounts and relatively high FoMO.

evidence.description: Parent and adolescent reports of the number of adolescents' social media accounts were moderately correlated with parent-reported DSM-5 symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity, ODD, anxiety, and depressive symptoms.
Parent and adolescent reports of the number of adolescents' social media accounts were moderately correlated with adolescent-reported fear of missing out (FoMO) and loneliness.
Lastly, anxiety and depressive symptoms were highest among adolescents with a relatively high number of parent-reported social media accounts and relatively high FoMO.

methodologies.name: Parent-adolescent dyad survey study
methodologies.description: Cross-sectional survey of parent-adolescent dyads examining social media account numbers alongside reported DSM-5 mental health symptoms, FoMO, and loneliness.

future_work.text: Conduct related longitudinal studies to evaluate causal or temporal relationships between social media use, FoMO, and adolescent mental health.
